title: Close off a terminal strip: fit and tighten an end bracket on a loose DIN rail
instruction: Hold the DIN rail down with one arm. With the other, put the end bracket on the rail against the right end of the row of beige terminal blocks, push it flush, and tighten its screw with the screwdriver to 0.5 Nm.
context: Terminal blocks sit side by side on a DIN rail, and each end of the row is closed off by an end bracket clamped against the last block so the row can't creep along the rail; on a loose rail one hand steadies the rail while the other fits the bracket and tightens its screw.
setup: Running left to right on the table, centred 0.30 m in front of the arm bases on their midline: a loose steel TS35 x 7.5 top-hat DIN rail, 240 mm long, lying web-down (open side up), 130 g with its blocks. On it: a row of four touching beige polyamide screw-clamp terminal blocks (each 5.2 mm thick along the rail, 52 mm across it, 40 mm tall above it), the rightmost centred on the rail; no end brackets. Standing on its two feet 0.20 m forward and 0.17 m right of the midline, faces to the left and right: a dark beige polyamide screw-fixed end bracket (8 x 56 x 46 mm, 14 g), its M4 slotted clamping screw on top backed out; underneath, a fixed hook on one side and a screw-driven clamping jaw on the other. Lying 0.27 m forward and 0.27 m right of the midline, along the forward direction with its tip toward the arms: a stubby flat-blade screwdriver (0.8 x 4.0 mm blade, 4 mm steel shaft 25 mm long, red 26 x 50 mm handle, 85 mm overall, 30 g). The bracket goes on from the rail's free right end, slid on with its hook under one lip (or hooked under one lip and tilted down); the jaw touches the far lip after about 1.4 turns, and 0.5 Nm is reached at about 1.6-1.8 turns.
scoring: At the end of the run: 1.0 if the bracket is flush against the row's last beige block (gap 0.5 mm or less at four points of its facing side: near both ends, low and high), its screw tightened to 0.5 Nm, and it stays still for 1 s; 0.75 flush, not tightened; 0.5 seated on the rail right of the row (seat on both lips from 0.5 mm below to 1.0 mm above them, which needs the hook under the lip; centred within 1 mm; square and level within 3 degrees); 0.25 the bracket lifted 25 mm or more above the table; else 0. If the rail moved 10 mm or more or turned 3 degrees or more from its start: no success, score capped at 0.25.
reset_notes: Put the rail back; loosen the bracket's screw about 2 turns (jaw fully retracted), slide the bracket off the rail's free end, and put it and the screwdriver back where they started.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz on CPU (-E device=cpu; on GPU the blade doesn't turn the screw). Rail lips 2 mm (real: 1 mm) against tunnelling. Bracket and blocks are our own simplified designs (no third-party CAD), incl. the bracket's hook and wedge-driven jaw. Thread = joint coupling (1.3 mm jaw travel/turn), 0.03 Nm friction; tight = 1.6 turns with the jaw pressing, standing in for 0.5 Nm: torque and clamp are far lower than real (holds ~2 N along the rail). Blocks are fixed to the rail.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 2,187); rail not held: 0.0 (rail moved 105 mm); never tightened: 0.75; screwed 20 mm short of the row: 0.5
